analysis: The code snippet calls `nextToken()` on a `StringTokenizer` object within two `while` loops. Each `while` loop checks `tokenizer.hasMoreTokens()` before calling `nextToken()`. According to the API documentation, `nextToken()` throws a `NoSuchElementException` if there are no more tokens. Since the `while` condition guarantees that there is at least one token remaining when `nextToken()` is called, the throwing condition for `NoSuchElementException` is fully avoided in this context.
remark: The `NoSuchElementException` from `nextToken()` is avoided because each call is guarded by a `while` loop that checks `hasMoreTokens()` first. Since `hasMoreTokens()` returns `false` only when there are no tokens left, the loop body (and thus the call to `nextToken()`) is only executed when there is at least one token, preventing the exception.
